comment: The section makes an important distinction between probabilistic inference and functions for which identical inputs should yield identical outputs. It also identifies machine-readable specifications and metadata as a developing readiness practice. This distinction could be strengthened without implying that all AI outputs should be deterministic.

reviewer.name: Timothy W. Cook; Luciana Cavalini, MD, PhD (co-author)

anchor.note: p.106 l.85-91, 99-102, 103-106 read as the printed page; section 5.2 agrees

public.text: The section makes an important distinction between probabilistic inference and functions for which identical inputs should yield identical outputs. It also identifies machine-readable specifications and metadata as a developing readiness practice. This distinction could be strengthened without implying that all AI outputs should be deterministic.
public.suggestedRevision: State as a recommended AI-readiness practice that deterministic subtasks should, where feasible, be delegated to governed authoritative services, while machine-readable specifications and metadata should support automated discovery and interpretation of those services. Reserve probabilistic model inference for tasks that genuinely benefit from it.
